name: hazel_weir_velocity_procedural_graph
description: Optimized Procedural Graph featuring progressive 16-plot synchronous scaling, in-situ harvest-watering execution, growth-feasibility town shop arbitrage, Day-18 perennial cutoff, and calibrated margin-defending liquidations.

nodes.name: State & Balance Audit
nodes.description: Computes net available cash, shed fill percentage, wage liability, active shop contract demand and maturation deadline feasibility, and oracle price drop signals across market commodities.

nodes.name: Midnight Wage Reserve Defense
nodes.description: Protects payroll for all active hired hands. Enforces dynamic cash reserve locks and triggers pre-midnight surplus liquidation to prevent the 0-hand bankruptcy cascade.

nodes.name: Town Shop Demand Arbitrage
nodes.description: Fulfills active town shop contracts for 2.0x-3.5x premiums with strict growth-deadline feasibility gating. Procures exact seed quantities strictly when crop growth duration fits within contract deadlines, while immediately delivering available matching inventory and routing uncontracted surplus to open-market sales.

nodes.name: Capital Velocity & Liquidation
nodes.description: Abolishes shed hoarding by executing continuous batch liquidations of uncontracted surplus inventory at favorable market prices, unlocking fluid cash for reinvestment and preventing idle physical stock from bottlenecking farm economy compounding.

nodes.name: Oracle Opponent Front-Run
nodes.description: Reads 96-step TTM forecast to dump sensitive commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) immediately before confirmed opponent market gluts collapse prices.

nodes.name: Capital Reinvestment & Yield Scaling
nodes.description: Reinvests surplus cash into synchronous workforce scaling (up to 10-11 hands) and progressive contiguous land expansion (up to 16 contiguous plots by Day 14), transitioning to hyper-fertilized multi-harvest Strawberries through Day 18, followed by a strict Day-18 perennial cutoff pivoting late uncultivated plots to rapid 3-day Carrots.

nodes.name: Routine Farm & Workforce Execution
nodes.description: Executes field routines with in-situ plot servicing and cluster harvesting. Workers harvest and immediately water each plot in-situ to eliminate growth-pausing dry intervals, batching carried harvests up to bag capacity before shed drop-off.

attributes.guidance: Cancel non-essential purchases; schedule worker harvest drop-offs before hour 21; enforce emergency liquidation of non-feed, non-contract inventory at hour >= 20 to guarantee payroll.
attributes.pitfalls: Never sell Wheat below dynamic livestock feed reserve (max(0, n_animals * 3)); never liquidate crops committed to active, deliverable town shop contracts.

attributes.condition: has_unlocked_shops and (shop_deliverable_inventory > 0 or (net_available_cash >= 180.0 and active_shop_demand > 0 and (current_day + shop_crop_growth_days <= shop_contract_deadline_day) and (current_day + shop_crop_growth_days <= 29))) and day <= 30
attributes.guidance: Allocate market slots to deliver exact matching inventory to town shops for 2.0x-3.5x premium through step 710. Only procure shop seeds (Carrots, Tomatoes, Pumpkins) if active contract deadline allows full crop maturation (current_day + growth_days <= min(deadline_day, 29)). If growth duration exceeds the deadline, fulfill exclusively from existing shed stock or bypass seed purchase entirely.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not buy seeds for slow single-harvest crops (Pumpkins, Tomatoes) if the contract deadline expires before maturation; do not hoard inventory speculatively for future unrevealed contracts. Do not buy shop seeds if net cash falls below 1.25x midnight payroll.

attributes.guidance: Execute batch sales of unreserved, non-shop surplus holdings when market price >= 0.84 * base_price, or when shed occupancy hits 30% to maintain capital velocity. Relax price floor to 0.76 * base_price if shed_used >= 75% to prevent shed deadlocks without sacrificing margins. On Days 29-30, execute terminal sweep of all remaining unreserved stock to maximize cash score.
attributes.pitfalls: Never liquidate exact item quotas reserved for active town shop contracts. Never sell Wheat below dynamic livestock feed reserve (max(0, n_animals * 3)). Never panic-dump inventory below 0.76x base price prior to the terminal Day 29 sweep.

attributes.guidance: Preempt lowest-margin open orders; execute rapid batch liquidations of vulnerable commodities (Wool, Milk, Strawberry) when confirmed glut probability >= 0.50 while current market price remains favorable (>= 0.80 * base_price) before opponent dumping collapses market prices.
attributes.pitfalls: Do not panic-dump on statistical noise (glut risk < 0.50); do not sell into already collapsed sub-0.65 base price markets unless shed overflow is imminent; do not front-run commodities committed to active town shop contracts.

attributes.condition: net_available_cash >= midnight_payroll_due * 1.5 + 100.0 and (hired_hands < 11 or uncultivated_plots > 0 or has_fertilizer_deficit or (contiguous_plots < 16 and day <= 14)) and day <= 27
attributes.guidance: Scale workforce synchronously with acreage: support 8-10 plots at 3-4 hands, 12-14 plots at 5-7 hands, reaching a firm ceiling of 16 contiguous plots (4x4 compact layout) by Day 14 at 8-11 hands. Transition 100% of newly expanded acreage to hyper-fertilized Strawberries during Days 5-18 to capture 5-7 compounding harvest cycles. Enact a strict perennial cutoff after Day 18: ban new Strawberry planting and fertilizer purchasing, routing all post-Day-18 uncultivated plots exclusively to rapid 3-day Carrots or feasible town shop contracts.
attributes.pitfalls: Never expand beyond 16 plots or after Day 14 to avoid worker dispersion and high clearing overhead. Never purchase Strawberry seeds or new plot fertilizer after Day 18, as late-planted perennials fail to amortize seed costs before Day 30. Maintain active daily watering for all existing Strawberry bushes through Day 30.

attributes.guidance: Execute in-situ field pipeline: 1) Harvest ripe plot, 2) Immediately water that exact plot in-situ before taking a step (zero transit cost, eliminating dry-interval pauses on perennial regrowth), 3) Cluster harvest and water adjacent ripe plots until worker bag capacity is reached (3-4 items), 4) Route directly to shed for deposit, 5) Feed livestock if dynamic feed reserve is present, 6) Pull seeds/fertilizer on shed departure only when traveling toward unserviced plots, 7) Plant/till uncultivated plots. Ensure all carried inventory is deposited in shed by step 716.
attributes.pitfalls: Never harvest a plot and leave it unwatered, as dry intervals freeze crop regrowth timers. Never route workers to shed with only 1 crop when adjacent ripe plots can be cluster harvested. Do not allow workers to carry seeds/fertilizer while cluster harvesting ripe fields.
